query_ground_truth.workflow_task: Manage a GitHub repository workflow: authenticate, inspect organization/repository access, create and label pull requests, inspect CI and workflow logs, merge approved changes, dispatch build/deploy/destroy workflows, and troubleshoot deployment failures.
query_ground_truth.intent: Trigger GitHub Actions workflows manually for building, deploying, or destroying infrastructure.

requirement_groups.purpose: manually trigger build, deploy, or destroy workflows

results.execution_guidance: Found 4 tools for this query. Look at the schemas to know how to use them.

toolkit_connection_statuses.description: GitHub is a code hosting platform for version control and collaboration, offering Git-based repository management, issue tracking, and continuous integration features
toolkit_connection_statuses.status_message: No Active connection for toolkit=github. You MUST call COMPOSIO_MANAGE_CONNECTIONS (toolkit="github") to create a connection BEFORE executing any github tools.

GITHUB_CREATE_A_WORKFLOW_DISPATCH_EVENT.description: Manually triggers a GitHub Actions workflow identified by `workflow_id` at a given `ref`, if the workflow is configured to accept `workflow_dispatch` events.

ref.description: Git reference (branch or tag) for the workflow.

owner.description: Owner of the repository (username or organization, case-insensitive).

inputs.description: JSON string containing key-value inputs for the workflow, matching `on.workflow_dispatch.inputs` definitions (max 10); uses workflow defaults if omitted. Example: '{"actor": "mona", "environment": "production"}'

workflow_id.description: Identifier of the workflow: numeric ID or just the filename (e.g., 'main.yml'). If a full path like '.github/workflows/main.yml' is provided, the prefix is automatically stripped.

GITHUB_GET_A_WORKFLOW.description: Retrieves detailed information for a specific GitHub Actions workflow in a repository, identified by either its numeric ID or its filename.

repo.description: Name of the repository, without the `.git` extension (case-insensitive).

owner.description: Username or organization name owning the repository (case-insensitive).

workflow_id.description: Unique numeric identifier of the workflow; use this or `workflow_name`.

workflow_name.description: Full name of the workflow file (e.g., `ci.yml`); use this or `workflow_id`.

GITHUB_LIST_WORKFLOW_RUNS_FOR_A_REPOSITO.description: Lists workflow runs for a repository, allowing filtering by actor, branch, event, status, creation date, check suite ID, or head SHA; the repository must exist and be accessible.

page.description: Page number of the results to fetch.

repo.description: The name of the repository, without the `.git` extension (not case-sensitive).

actor.description: Filter by the actor's login (e.g., the user who triggered the `push`).

event.description: Filter by the event that triggered the workflow (e.g., `push`, `pull_request`).

owner.description: The account owner of the repository (not case-sensitive).

branch.description: Filter by branch name (e.g., `main` or the branch that triggered the `push`).

status.description: Filter by `status` or `conclusion` (e.g., `success`, `in_progress`). Note: Only GitHub Actions can set `waiting`, `pending`, or `requested`.

created.description: Filter by creation date or date-time range (ISO8601 format: YYYY-MM-DD or YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ). Supports operators like `>`, `<`, `>=`, `<=`, and `..` for ranges.

head_sha.description: Filter to include only runs associated with the specified `head_sha` (commit SHA at the head of the branch).

exclude_pull_requests.description: Set to `true` to exclude workflow runs triggered by pull request events. Omit or leave as null to include all runs.

GITHUB_GET_A_WORKFLOW_RUN.description: Gets a specific workflow run by its ID from a GitHub repository.
